note: Supplementary diagnostic for the stiff_exotherm case in snn_solve_diagnostics.json. Traced with backend='python', record_trajectory=True (numerically identical to backend='c' per snn_opt docs; only instrumentation config differs -- no solver-equation change). Sampled checkpoints only, not the full 8001-length trajectory.
finding: Cold-start point is already violated by ~1.74e12 (constraint residual) before any iteration runs -- an artifact of Ap^20 amplification at rho=1.55, not a solver defect. The very first gradient step sends |x| from 1.1e4 to 2.98e6. max_violation is IDENTICAL (1.7427e12) at every single checkpoint from iter 0 through iter 8000 despite |x| growing 1000x over that span, and n_projections stays exactly 0 for the entire run -- meaning the adaptive projection's own residual check never once triggers a correction, even though an independent recomputation of C_s@x+d_s on the same points shows the same enormous violation throughout. This is either (a) the projection loop genuinely finding a direction where all 120 constraint rows read satisfied simultaneously despite the point being wildly infeasible in aggregate box-bound terms (geometrically possible but suspicious), or (b) a precision/bookkeeping artifact in the event-driven incremental residual tracking (g <- g - k1*G[:,j] via the precomputed Gram matrix) decoupling from the true residual under this magnitude. Not resolved further in this pass -- flagged as the primary numerical bottleneck, root cause unconfirmed beyond this evidence.
